findings.rootCause: LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.rewriteSmallLiteralFilterAnchors treated a SameTerm condition like Compare.EQ: isSmallLiteralAnchorCandidate accepts SameTerm, LmdbJoinPlanSupport.smallLiteralFilterAnchor/collectOrEqualityAnchorValues collect its constants, canMaterializeObjectFilterAnchor only inspects the predicate guarantee (never the operator), expandFiniteAnchor then value-expands integers (whole canonical-integer family), booleans ({true,1}) and normalises dateTime to the Z form, and the condition is dropped because remainingConditions is empty. sameTerm(?o, 7) therefore matched the stored, value-equal but non-identical term "7"^^xsd:int; reachable e2e through the OPTIONAL->INNER path (SameTermFilterOptimizer declines under a LeftJoin, and the :1178 safe-values shortcut does not apply to numerics/booleans/calendars).
findings.change: Following the critique's major issue (the design's TERM classification with an unexpanded anchor would lose rows for mixed disjunctions such as sameTerm(?o,7) || ?o = 8), the rule is inverted: LmdbJoinPlanSupport.containsSameTerm(ValueExpr) (SameTerm anywhere in the Or/And tree) plus LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.requiresTermIdentityFilter(condition, anchor) (containsSameTerm AND the anchor holds a guarantee-only value, i.e. numeric/boolean/calendar) make rewriteSmallLiteralFilterAnchors RETAIN the condition while keeping the value-expanded anchor as a sound superset pre-filter; the anchor gets an LmdbRewriteProof with facts termEquality|valueEqualitySuperset|originalFilterRetained. sameTerm over safe values (IRI, plain/lang string) is unchanged (term join == sameTerm); Compare.EQ/IN behaviour is unchanged (guarded by expandsCanonicalIntegerEqualityAnchorAndDropsFilter). exactStoredTermFilterAnchor already retained the condition and needed no change.

findings.rootCause: RdfTermDomain had canonicity facts for integers/dateTime/date but none for xsd:boolean; LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.canMaterializeObjectFilterAnchor gated the boolean anchor on hasDatatype(BOOLEAN) + valid anchor values only, and expandFiniteAnchor/addBooleanAnchorValues materialised {"true","1"} and dropped the filter. A stored " true "^^xsd:boolean (valid under whiteSpace=collapse, value-equal to true, returned by the oracle) is neither term, so the row was lost; the packed range-anchor rule (PackedLogicalRuleProgram.expandAnchorValue) had the same gap (datatype-only proof).
findings.change: Added RdfTermDomain.Fact.CANONICAL_BOOLEAN (appended after CANONICAL_DATE; member of UNIVERSAL_FACT_MASK so joinObserved ANDs it; classifyMask sets it only for the exact labels true/false/1/0; isContradictory flags CANONICAL_BOOLEAN without the BOOLEAN datatype). canMaterializeObjectFilterAnchor's boolean branch now also requires guarantee.has(CANONICAL_BOOLEAN). Because Fact ordinals shift the persisted datatype bits, TripleStore.PREDICATE_OBJECT_DOMAINS_VERSION bumped rdf-term-domain-v4 -> v5 (rebuild on open; with predicateGuaranteeIndexAutoRebuild=false the guarantees are cleared and the filters are simply retained - both upgrade paths tested, per critique minor #7). Exported to the packed planner: PackedPredicateRange.UNIVERSAL_CANONICAL_BOOLEAN (1<<4), LmdbPackedPredicateRangeProvider maps the fact, PackedPredicateRangeArena widens the universal-bit field from 4 to 5 bits (flags moved from bits 11/12 to 12/13, in-memory layout only), and PackedLogicalRuleProgram.expandAnchorValue returns -1 (no safe expansion, filter kept) without the proof. Resumed-attempt corrections: the two new LmdbPredicateObjectDomainIndexTest upgrade/degradation tests asserted that no finite anchor may appear, but the plans they rejected retained the Compare (=) filter next to an exact-stored-term anchor (proofFacts originalFilterRetained|exactStoredTermSupport), which is sound; they now assert the retained filter and permit an anchor only with originalFilterRetained. The PackedPredicateRangePlanningTest regression guard built its expected set with ValueFactory.createLiteral(String, CoreDatatype), which canonicalises "1"^^xsd:boolean to the shared TRUE literal (duplicate element); it now uses the IRI overload like the rule.

findings.rootCause: TripleStore.commitDurableStatementBatch ordered flushPendingRdfTermDomains() -> mdb_txn_commit(txn) -> applyPendingRdfTermDomainCacheUpdates(), so the volatile predicateObjectDomainCache the planner reads (getKnownRdfTermDomain via LmdbEstimatorStorageAccess.rdfTermDomain) was swapped only after the committed rows became visible to new read transactions; TxnManager.createReadTxn takes no lock against this ordering. A query that opened its snapshot in that window planned a "05"^^xsd:int row under the stale CANONICAL_INTEGER guarantee and a finite anchor dropped it. Incremental updates only weaken (joinObserved / deletes), so 'data newer than guarantee' is the only unsafe direction.
findings.change: commitDurableStatementBatch now publishes the pending cache updates BEFORE mdb_txn_commit whenever the batch cannot strengthen a guarantee (a weaker-than-disk heap cache after a failed commit is sound; the post-commit call at the resize/else branches stays and is idempotent). A new flag pendingRdfTermDomainCacheMayStrengthen is set by rebuildRdfTermDomain(long) and stageRdfTermDomainCacheClear() (the only paths that recompute, hence may strengthen, guarantees; both reached from initializeRdfTermDomains at open) and reset in clearPendingRdfTermDomainCacheUpdates; such batches keep post-commit publication. This deviates from the critique's minor suggestion (publish before commit unconditionally + javadoc): the flag turns the 'future strengthening paths must publish after commit' rule into code instead of a comment, at the cost of one boolean. A package-private volatile test seam durableCommitBarrierForTesting runs right after mdb_txn_commit so a test can observe the cache at the first instant readers can see the rows (a read txn cannot be opened from inside the barrier because the writer holds the txn-manager lock, so the test observes the heap cache and verifies row visibility afterwards).
